verdict: 2026-07-29 10:36 PDT — A dedicated ROADMAP.md and README-canonical purpose statement are modern, appropriate choices, but I would not build the roadmap and optional linter exactly as sketched. ARCHITECTURE should point explicitly to README’s purpose and state only architecture-specific consequences; workflow-protocol.md needs no additional copy.

findings.title: ROADMAP would hand-copy lifecycle state
findings.locus: Design sketch — `ROADMAP.md = one screen, references not copies`
findings.claim: The four hand-maintained buckets duplicate status already owned by BACKLOG.md and, for shipped state, explicitly owned by git under the protocol’s declared-vs-observed doctrine. Links avoid copying item bodies, but labels such as shipped, in-progress, and parked still copy the mutable fact. Partially delivered work such as OPS-12 and OPS-13 makes that shadow status especially likely to drift.
findings.alternative: Keep ROADMAP.md as a strategic view of themes, intended directions, and unresolved decisions. Link to BACKLOG.md for operational state and to the README feature map/git history for shipped capability. If exact four-bucket status is mandatory, generate that view from canonical structured metadata and git rather than maintaining it by hand.
findings.win: Eliminates a second writer for lifecycle state and prevents ROADMAP.md from disagreeing with BACKLOG.md or the authoritative merge history.

findings.title: The linter pins prose shadows instead of authoritative invariants
findings.claim: Iterating `.claude/skills/*` treats source directories as the shipped inventory even though ARCHITECTURE.md names `install.sh`’s `ARTIFACTS` set as the deployment source of truth. Pinning purpose phrases and merely checking that ROADMAP.md mentions BACKLOG.md adds wording-coupled assertions of the kind OPS-17 identifies as a drift source; those checks can pass while the prose is wrong and fail after an accurate rephrase.
findings.alternative: If the linter is adopted, keep it drift-only and enforce one useful invariant: derive deployed skill names from `install.sh`’s `ARTIFACTS` entries and assert that each is represented in README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md. Optionally cross-check those entries against skill directories. Leave purpose and roadmap semantics to independent review unless they later gain structured source data.
findings.win: Still prevents another deployed-but-undocumented skill, while removing brittle phrase pins, false confidence, and most of the proposed linter’s maintenance surface.
